The polar curve $r=12$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{7\pi }{6}$ intersect at the point $P,$ as shown above. What are the Cartesian coordinates of $P?$

Given that the ray above passes through the point with Cartesian coordinates $(4,-4)$, find the polar equation of the ray.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the reference angle associated with the point:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\theta }_{R} & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{y}{x}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡|\frac{-4}{4}| \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡1 \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the ray lies in the fourth quadrant. So, we find the angle in the fourth quadrant that has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\theta  & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the polar equation of the ray is 

$$
\theta =\frac{7\pi }{4}.
$$
